goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
goldens.reasoning: Both point out that the same metric uses the tag 'shard' in some places and 'shards' in others.

goldens.comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
goldens.reasoning: Both point out that time.sleep is patched to a no-op, so the later sleep doesn't wait.

goldens.comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
goldens.reasoning: Both point out that the isinstance check fails for processes created with the spawn context.

goldens.comment: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
goldens.reasoning: This is the same issue as G2: the monkeypatched sleep doesn't actually wait.

goldens.comment: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
goldens.reasoning: Both point out that breaking out on timeout skips terminating the remaining processes.

candidates: Inconsistent metric tag key naming: timer uses 'shards' but produce timer/segment-size metric uses 'shard', which will split metric series and complicate dashboards
time.sleep(0.1) is patched to a no-op at the top of the test, so it doesn't actually wait for the flusher to observe the drift change, making the test timing-dependent/flaky on slower CI

isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard may not match processes created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, causing hung children to not be killed before replacement and leaking flusher workers
When timeout elapses in join(), the break exits the loop without terminating remaining flusher processes, leaving background workers running during shutdown/rebalance
--flusher-processes accepts negative integers which can make SpanFlusher.num_processes invalid and crash shard-to-process mapping/modulo at startup - should enforce minimum of 1
